sessions.prompt: My landlord is refusing to return my security deposit.

response.summary: Security deposit dispute with your landlord regarding unpaid return of deposits.
response.clarificationNeeded: 1. Did you provide a formal written vacancy notice? 2. Is there a signed tenancy agreement? 3. Has the landlord provided a written list of deductions?
response.explanation: Under the Model Tenancy Act guidelines, a landlord must return the advance security deposit within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises. Deductions are only permitted for actual damage or unpaid dues, not for normal wear and tear.
nextSteps: Send a written demand notice requesting the return of the deposit within 15 days.
Compile evidence including the tenancy agreement, bank transactions, and photos of the vacant room.
If the landlord refuses, prepare a petition to be filed before the local Rent Authority/Tribunal.
documentsNeeded: Rent Receipts / Bank statement showing deposit payment

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

[Office of the Public Works Department / Municipal Corporation],

Subject: Request for Information under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

Sir/Madam,

I, a citizen of India, hereby request the following information regarding the road construction and funds spent in my locality:

Address: Delhi
Phone: [Your Contact Number]

Submit via Registered Post/Speed Post to the correct PIO or file online at rtionline.gov.in.

sources.title: Filing RTI for Local Road Construction and Fund Allocation
sources.authority: Central Information Commission / Right to Information Act 2005
guidelines: Under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act 2005, a citizen can request details about expenditures, copies of work orders, measurement books (MB), and completion certificates.
Be specific about the road name, ward number, locality, and the exact years or date range.
Do not ask for reasons or opinions; ask for records, documents, contracts, or file notes.
Address the application to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the respective public authority (e.g. Executive Engineer, PWD or Ward Assistant Commissioner).
sample_questions: What is the total budget allocated and sanctioned for the construction/repair of [Road Name/Locality] during the period [Start Year] to [End Year]?
Please provide a certified copy of the Work Order, Tender Document, and agreement signed with the contractor for the aforementioned work.
Please provide the copy of the completion certificate and measurement book entries for this work.
If the road has developed potholes/cracks, please provide the details of the liability period of the contractor and what action has been taken by the department.

response.disclaimer: This is a draft RTI application requiring your review and verification. Ensure all local names and addresses are filled out accurately.

sources.title: Filing RTI for Local Road Construction and Fund Allocation
sources.authority: Central Information Commission / Right to Information Act 2005
guidelines: Under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act 2005, a citizen can request details about expenditures, copies of work orders, measurement books (MB), and completion certificates.
Be specific about the road name, ward number, locality, and the exact years or date range.

Address the application to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the respective public authority (e.g. Executive Engineer, PWD or Ward Assistant Commissioner).

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

response.clarificationNeeded: What is the specific municipal ward number, PWD region, or locality name, and what years/period of construction details are you requesting?
response.subject: Information request under Section 6(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 regarding local road construction and fund allocation.
response.targetAuthority: [Needs your input: Target PIO Office (e.g. Executive Engineer, PWD / Ward Assistant Commissioner)]
response.rtiDraft:
To,
The Public Information Officer,
[Needs your input: Public Authority Department Office Name],
[Needs your input: City / District / State]

Subject: Request for Information under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

Sir/Madam,

I, a citizen of India, hereby request the following information regarding the road construction and funds spent in my locality:

1. Please provide details of total budget allocated, sanctioned, and released for road construction, repair, and resurfacing in [Needs your input: Locality Name / Ward Number] during the last 3 financial years.
2. Please provide a copy of the Work Order, Tender Notice, and completion certificate for work done on [Needs your input: Specific Road Name] in the past 24 months.
3. What is the name of the contractor/agency selected for this road work, and what is the specified defect liability period?
4. Please provide a copy of the measurement book entries corresponding to this construction.

Please provide the information in print format. I am enclosing the RTI Application Fee of Rs. 10/- via Postal Order/Demand Draft.

Date: 19/8/2026
Place: [Needs your input: Your City]

Applicant:
Name: [Needs your input: Applicant Name]
Address: [Needs your input: Applicant Complete Address]
Phone: [Needs your input: Applicant Contact Number]
instructions: Buy a Rs. 10 Court Fee Stamp or Postal Order (IPO) payable to the Accounts Officer of the public authority.
Fill in your name and address in the placeholders in the draft above.
Submit via Registered Post/Speed Post to the correct PIO or file online at rtionline.gov.in.

sources.title: Filing RTI for Local Road Construction and Fund Allocation
sources.authority: Central Information Commission / Right to Information Act 2005
guidelines: Under Section 6(1) of the RTI Act 2005, a citizen can request details about expenditures, copies of work orders, measurement books (MB), and completion certificates.
Be specific about the road name, ward number, locality, and the exact years or date range.
Do not ask for reasons or opinions; ask for records, documents, contracts, or file notes.
Address the application to the Public Information Officer (PIO) of the respective public authority (e.g. Executive Engineer, PWD or Ward Assistant Commissioner).
sample_questions: What is the total budget allocated and sanctioned for the construction/repair of [Road Name/Locality] during the period [Start Year] to [End Year]?
Please provide a certified copy of the Work Order, Tender Document, and agreement signed with the contractor for the aforementioned work.
Please provide the copy of the completion certificate and measurement book entries for this work.
If the road has developed potholes/cracks, please provide the details of the liability period of the contractor and what action has been taken by the department.

sessions.prompt: My landlord has not returned my security deposit.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You vacated your rented room, but the landlord is withholding the refund of your advance security deposit without valid justification.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act guidelines, advance security deposits for residential properties are capped at a maximum of two months' rent. The landlord is legally required to refund the deposit upon taking over vacant possession.
response.why: A landlord may make deductions only for outstanding utility bills, unpaid rent, or actual tenant-caused damage. Deductions for normal wear and tear (like standard paint weathering) are not permitted. If deductions are made without a written itemized list or if the refund is withheld beyond 30 days, the tenant can approach the local Rent Tribunal.
whatYouMayDoNext: Send a written demand notice requesting the return of the deposit within 15 days.
Compile receipts showing deposit payments, tenancy agreements, and pictures of the vacant room.
File a formal dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Rent Receipts / Bank statement showing deposit payment
response.importantLimitations: This is a general guide. Tenancy laws vary by state jurisdictions. If your agreement was not registered, local civil courts or mediation centers may apply instead of the specialized Rent Authority.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

sources.title: Consumer Product Refund and Protection Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (Consumer Protection Act 2019)
sources.content: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a consumer has the right to be protected against marketing of goods and services which are hazardous to life and property, the right to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price, and the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation. Unfair trade practices include refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof within the period stipulated in the bill or within 30 days if no period is stipulated. Consumers can file formal complaints online through the National Consumer Helpline portal (E-Daakhil) or approach the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, employers are obligated to pay all wages in cash, cheque, or bank transfer in a timely manner (by the 7th of the following month for establishments with < 1000 workers).

response.importantLimitations: This Act primarily covers employees drawing salary below specified statutory thresholds. Higher-earning executives may need to seek recovery via standard civil suit litigation or arbitration panels.

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.title: Filing Complaints Against Police Misconduct
sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.
sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. A citizen can file a written complaint before the PCA against police officers for: (a) excessive use of physical force; (b) illegal arrest or detention; (c) extortion or threat/intimidation; (d) custodial death or grievous hurt. sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)

If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)

In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.summary: Municipal bodies are legally responsible for timely door-to-door garbage collection and clearing local waste bins.

sources.title: Filing Complaints Against Police Misconduct
sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.
sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. A citizen can file a written complaint before the PCA against police officers for: (a) excessive use of physical force; (b) illegal arrest or detention; (c) extortion or threat/intimidation; (d) custodial death or grievous hurt. The complaint must contain the name/designation of the officer, Station name, Date & Time of occurrence, Description of abuse, and supporting proof (such as medical reports, photos, or video recordings). Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

sources.title: Consumer Product Refund and Protection Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (Consumer Protection Act 2019)
sources.content: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a consumer has the right to be protected against marketing of goods and services which are hazardous to life and property, the right to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price, and the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation. Unfair trade practices include refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof within the period stipulated in the bill or within 30 days if no period is stipulated. Consumers can file formal complaints online through the National Consumer Helpline portal (E-Daakhil) or approach the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

sources.summary: PWD and municipal corporations are responsible for pothole repair, road maintenance, and restoring broken streets.

sources.title: Grievances for Municipal Solid Waste and Garbage Collection
sources.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Solid Waste Management Rules 2016)
sources.summary: Municipal bodies are legally responsible for timely door-to-door garbage collection and clearing local waste bins.
sources.content: According to the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2016, municipal corporations and local urban bodies are legally obligated to organize door-to-door collection of segregated waste, establish daily waste collection services, and clear local street bins. Open dumping of municipal refuse or garbage accumulation is prohibited. If waste is not cleared, citizens have the right to submit a complaint. sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)

If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

response.why: A complaint can be filed before the PCA for grievances like custodial excess, grievous hurt, extortion, or abuse of power. CPGRAMS and departmental vigilance units also accept grievances. The complaint must contain specific officer details and supporting medical or media records.
whatYouMayDoNext: Record all incident details immediately, including date, time, officer names, belt numbers, and witness contacts.

sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.

Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, employers are obligated to pay all wages in cash, cheque, or bank transfer in a timely manner (by the 7th of the following month for establishments with < 1000 workers).
response.why: Section 7 strictly limits authorized deductions. Withholding salary due to arbitrary disputes is illegal. Workers are entitled to receive full wages along with compensation for delayed payments by submitting claims to the regional labour department.
whatYouMayDoNext: Send a written salary demand letter to your employer via registered post/email.
Gather employment details, appointment letters, salary slips, and attendance sheets.
Submit a formal complaint claim under Section 15 of the Act to the Labour Commissioner.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Attendance records or emails showing work completed
response.importantLimitations: This Act primarily covers employees drawing salary below specified statutory thresholds. Higher-earning executives may need to seek recovery via standard civil suit litigation or arbitration panels.

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

response.why: A landlord may make deductions only for outstanding utility bills, unpaid rent, or actual tenant-caused damage. Deductions for normal wear and tear (like standard paint weathering) are not permitted. If deductions are made without a written itemized list or if the refund is withheld beyond 30 days, the tenant can approach the local Rent Tribunal.

Compile receipts showing deposit payments, tenancy agreements, and pictures of the vacant room.
File a formal dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Rent Receipts / Bank statement showing deposit payment
response.importantLimitations: This is a general guide. Tenancy laws vary by state jurisdictions. If your agreement was not registered, local civil courts or mediation centers may apply instead of the specialized Rent Authority.

sessions.prompt: My phone seller refuses a refund.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You purchased a product (like a phone) online, and the seller is refusing to issue a refund or replacement for a defective item.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, citizens are protected against unfair trade practices and receiving defective goods. E-commerce platforms are mandated to resolve consumer grievances.
response.why: Section 2(47) defines refusing to take back defective goods or refund money within 30 days as an unfair trade practice. Consumers are entitled to seek relief by registering complaints on the National Consumer Helpline or filing petitions before the Consumer Commission.
whatYouMayDoNext: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or register an online complaint on the INGRAM portal.
Send a formal written notice to the e-commerce company's grievance officer demanding a refund within 7 days.
If unresolved, file an e-daakhil case before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Chat logs, emails, or call records with customer support
Copy of the return policy terms
response.importantLimitations: The Consumer Protection Act applies only if you bought the product for personal use. Commercial purchases are excluded and fall under general contract litigation.

sources.title: Consumer Product Refund and Protection Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution (Consumer Protection Act 2019)
sources.content: Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a consumer has the right to be protected against marketing of goods and services which are hazardous to life and property, the right to be informed about quality, quantity, potency, purity, standard and price, and the right to seek redressal against unfair trade practices or unscrupulous exploitation. Unfair trade practices include refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof within the period stipulated in the bill or within 30 days if no period is stipulated. Consumers can file formal complaints online through the National Consumer Helpline portal (E-Daakhil) or approach the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission.

sessions.prompt: Police used excessive force during an incident.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting police misconduct, which may include the use of excessive physical force, threat/intimidation, or illegal detention.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Supreme Court guidelines on police reforms and respective state Police Acts, citizens are protected against police abuse of authority. Independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) are mandated at the state and district levels to investigate serious misconduct.
response.why: A complaint can be filed before the PCA for grievances like custodial excess, grievous hurt, extortion, or abuse of power. CPGRAMS and departmental vigilance units also accept grievances. The complaint must contain specific officer details and supporting medical or media records.
whatYouMayDoNext: Record all incident details immediately, including date, time, officer names, belt numbers, and witness contacts.
Seek medical attention immediately and secure a Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report if physical force was used.
File a written complaint with the Police Complaints Authority (PCA) or submit a grievance on CPGRAMS.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs or video/audio recordings of the incident
Copy of any arbitrary fine slips or seizure memos
response.importantLimitations: The PCA operates as a disciplinary audit authority. It can recommend suspensions or departmental actions but cannot directly award financial damages or cancel formal criminal charges (FIRs), which requires petitioning the High Court.

sources.title: Filing Complaints Against Police Misconduct
sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.
sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. A citizen can file a written complaint before the PCA against police officers for: (a) excessive use of physical force; (b) illegal arrest or detention; (c) extortion or threat/intimidation; (d) custodial death or grievous hurt. The complaint must contain the name/designation of the officer, Station name, Date & Time of occurrence, Description of abuse, and supporting proof (such as medical reports, photos, or video recordings). Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

sessions.prompt: Garbage hasn't been collected in my street.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting neglected municipal garbage collection or open waste dumping in your locality.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, municipal authorities have a statutory duty to collect segregated waste daily, clear public street bins, and maintain clean public areas.
response.why: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 legally obligate urban local bodies to organize waste transport and disposal. If local collectors fail to clear rubbish, citizens can file digital complaints on the national Swachhata app or escalate to the Ward Sanitary Inspector.
whatYouMayDoNext: Take geotagged photos of the accumulated garbage or open dump.
Submit a digital complaint ticket on the Swachhata App or the municipal e-district portal.
Coordinate with the local Resident Welfare Association (RWA) to file a group petition with the Ward Health Inspector.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs of waste accumulation with timestamp
Reference numbers of previous unanswered complaint tickets
Resident petition letters signed by neighbors
response.importantLimitations: Municipal response times can vary depending on local budget allocations and outsourced contractor worker availability. Severe structural issues may require higher municipal health commissioner escalations.

sources.title: Grievances for Municipal Solid Waste and Garbage Collection
sources.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Solid Waste Management Rules 2016)
sources.summary: Municipal bodies are legally responsible for timely door-to-door garbage collection and clearing local waste bins.
sources.content: According to the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2016, municipal corporations and local urban bodies are legally obligated to organize door-to-door collection of segregated waste, establish daily waste collection services, and clear local street bins. Open dumping of municipal refuse or garbage accumulation is prohibited. If waste is not cleared, citizens have the right to submit a complaint. The primary action paths include registering grievances on the national Swachhata mobile app, submitting portal tickets to the municipal corporation e-district site, or sending written complaints to the local Ward Health/Sanitary Inspector.

Actionable paths include uploading photo complaints to the local municipality app, submitting written complaints to the PWD Executive Engineer, or registering central escalations on the CPGRAMS portal.

sessions.prompt: My landlord hasn't returned my deposit.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You vacated your rented room, but the landlord is withholding the refund of your advance security deposit without valid justification.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act guidelines, advance security deposits for residential properties are capped at a maximum of two months' rent. The landlord is legally required to refund the deposit upon taking over vacant possession.
response.why: A landlord may make deductions only for outstanding utility bills, unpaid rent, or actual tenant-caused damage. Deductions for normal wear and tear (like standard paint weathering) are not permitted. If deductions are made without a written itemized list or if the refund is withheld beyond 30 days, the tenant can approach the local Rent Tribunal.
whatYouMayDoNext: Send a written demand notice requesting the return of the deposit within 15 days.
Compile receipts showing deposit payments, tenancy agreements, and pictures of the vacant room.
File a formal dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Rent Receipts / Bank statement showing deposit payment
response.importantLimitations: This is a general guide. Tenancy laws vary by state jurisdictions. If your agreement was not registered, local civil courts or mediation centers may apply instead of the specialized Rent Authority.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

sessions.prompt: Police used excessive force during an incident.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting police misconduct, which may include the use of excessive physical force, threat/intimidation, or illegal detention.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Supreme Court guidelines on police reforms and respective state Police Acts, citizens are protected against police abuse of authority. Independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) are mandated at the state and district levels to investigate serious misconduct.
response.why: A complaint can be filed before the PCA for grievances like custodial excess, grievous hurt, extortion, or abuse of power. CPGRAMS and departmental vigilance units also accept grievances. The complaint must contain specific officer details and supporting medical or media records.
whatYouMayDoNext: Record all incident details immediately, including date, time, officer names, belt numbers, and witness contacts.
Seek medical attention immediately and secure a Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report if physical force was used.
File a written complaint with the Police Complaints Authority (PCA) or submit a grievance on CPGRAMS.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs or video/audio recordings of the incident
Copy of any arbitrary fine slips or seizure memos
response.importantLimitations: The PCA operates as a disciplinary audit authority. It can recommend suspensions or departmental actions but cannot directly award financial damages or cancel formal criminal charges (FIRs), which requires petitioning the High Court.

sources.title: Filing Complaints Against Police Misconduct
sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.
sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. A citizen can file a written complaint before the PCA against police officers for: (a) excessive use of physical force; (b) illegal arrest or detention; (c) extortion or threat/intimidation; (d) custodial death or grievous hurt. The complaint must contain the name/designation of the officer, Station name, Date & Time of occurrence, Description of abuse, and supporting proof (such as medical reports, photos, or video recordings). Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

sessions.prompt: Garbage hasn't been collected in my street.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting neglected municipal garbage collection or open waste dumping in your locality.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, municipal authorities have a statutory duty to collect segregated waste daily, clear public street bins, and maintain clean public areas.
response.why: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 legally obligate urban local bodies to organize waste transport and disposal. If local collectors fail to clear rubbish, citizens can file digital complaints on the national Swachhata app or escalate to the Ward Sanitary Inspector.
whatYouMayDoNext: Take geotagged photos of the accumulated garbage or open dump.
Submit a digital complaint ticket on the Swachhata App or the municipal e-district portal.
Coordinate with the local Resident Welfare Association (RWA) to file a group petition with the Ward Health Inspector.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs of waste accumulation with timestamp
Reference numbers of previous unanswered complaint tickets
Resident petition letters signed by neighbors
response.importantLimitations: Municipal response times can vary depending on local budget allocations and outsourced contractor worker availability. Severe structural issues may require higher municipal health commissioner escalations.

sources.title: Grievances for Municipal Solid Waste and Garbage Collection
sources.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Solid Waste Management Rules 2016)
sources.summary: Municipal bodies are legally responsible for timely door-to-door garbage collection and clearing local waste bins.
sources.content: According to the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2016, municipal corporations and local urban bodies are legally obligated to organize door-to-door collection of segregated waste, establish daily waste collection services, and clear local street bins. Open dumping of municipal refuse or garbage accumulation is prohibited. If waste is not cleared, citizens have the right to submit a complaint. The primary action paths include registering grievances on the national Swachhata mobile app, submitting portal tickets to the municipal corporation e-district site, or sending written complaints to the local Ward Health/Sanitary Inspector.

sessions.prompt: My landlord hasn't returned my deposit.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You vacated your rented room, but the landlord is withholding the refund of your advance security deposit without valid justification.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act guidelines, advance security deposits for residential properties are capped at a maximum of two months' rent. The landlord is legally required to refund the deposit upon taking over vacant possession.
response.why: A landlord may make deductions only for outstanding utility bills, unpaid rent, or actual tenant-caused damage. Deductions for normal wear and tear (like standard paint weathering) are not permitted. If deductions are made without a written itemized list or if the refund is withheld beyond 30 days, the tenant can approach the local Rent Tribunal.
whatYouMayDoNext: Send a written demand notice requesting the return of the deposit within 15 days.
Compile receipts showing deposit payments, tenancy agreements, and pictures of the vacant room.
File a formal dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Rent Receipts / Bank statement showing deposit payment
response.importantLimitations: This is a general guide. Tenancy laws vary by state jurisdictions. If your agreement was not registered, local civil courts or mediation centers may apply instead of the specialized Rent Authority.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

sessions.prompt: Police used excessive force during an incident.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting police misconduct, which may include the use of excessive physical force, threat/intimidation, or illegal detention.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Supreme Court guidelines on police reforms and respective state Police Acts, citizens are protected against police abuse of authority. Independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) are mandated at the state and district levels to investigate serious misconduct.
response.why: A complaint can be filed before the PCA for grievances like custodial excess, grievous hurt, extortion, or abuse of power. CPGRAMS and departmental vigilance units also accept grievances. The complaint must contain specific officer details and supporting medical or media records.
whatYouMayDoNext: Record all incident details immediately, including date, time, officer names, belt numbers, and witness contacts.
Seek medical attention immediately and secure a Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report if physical force was used.
File a written complaint with the Police Complaints Authority (PCA) or submit a grievance on CPGRAMS.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs or video/audio recordings of the incident
Copy of any arbitrary fine slips or seizure memos
response.importantLimitations: The PCA operates as a disciplinary audit authority. It can recommend suspensions or departmental actions but cannot directly award financial damages or cancel formal criminal charges (FIRs), which requires petitioning the High Court.

sources.title: Filing Complaints Against Police Misconduct
sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.
sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. A citizen can file a written complaint before the PCA against police officers for: (a) excessive use of physical force; (b) illegal arrest or detention; (c) extortion or threat/intimidation; (d) custodial death or grievous hurt. The complaint must contain the name/designation of the officer, Station name, Date & Time of occurrence, Description of abuse, and supporting proof (such as medical reports, photos, or video recordings). Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

sessions.prompt: Garbage hasn't been collected in my street.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting neglected municipal garbage collection or open waste dumping in your locality.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, municipal authorities have a statutory duty to collect segregated waste daily, clear public street bins, and maintain clean public areas.
response.why: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016 legally obligate urban local bodies to organize waste transport and disposal. If local collectors fail to clear rubbish, citizens can file digital complaints on the national Swachhata app or escalate to the Ward Sanitary Inspector.
whatYouMayDoNext: Take geotagged photos of the accumulated garbage or open dump.
Submit a digital complaint ticket on the Swachhata App or the municipal e-district portal.

Resident petition letters signed by neighbors
response.importantLimitations: Municipal response times can vary depending on local budget allocations and outsourced contractor worker availability. Severe structural issues may require higher municipal health commissioner escalations.

sources.title: Grievances for Municipal Solid Waste and Garbage Collection
sources.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (Solid Waste Management Rules 2016)
sources.summary: Municipal bodies are legally responsible for timely door-to-door garbage collection and clearing local waste bins.
sources.content: According to the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2016, municipal corporations and local urban bodies are legally obligated to organize door-to-door collection of segregated waste, establish daily waste collection services, and clear local street bins. Open dumping of municipal refuse or garbage accumulation is prohibited. If waste is not cleared, citizens have the right to submit a complaint. The primary action paths include registering grievances on the national Swachhata mobile app, submitting portal tickets to the municipal corporation e-district site, or sending written complaints to the local Ward Health/Sanitary Inspector.

sessions.prompt: My landlord hasn't returned my deposit.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You vacated your rented room, but the landlord is withholding the refund of your advance security deposit without valid justification.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act guidelines, advance security deposits for residential properties are capped at a maximum of two months' rent. The landlord is legally required to refund the deposit upon taking over vacant possession.
response.why: A landlord may make deductions only for outstanding utility bills, unpaid rent, or actual tenant-caused damage. Deductions for normal wear and tear (like standard paint weathering) are not permitted. If deductions are made without a written itemized list or if the refund is withheld beyond 30 days, the tenant can approach the local Rent Tribunal.
whatYouMayDoNext: Send a written demand notice requesting the return of the deposit within 15 days.
Compile receipts showing deposit payments, tenancy agreements, and pictures of the vacant room.
File a formal dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Rent Receipts / Bank statement showing deposit payment
response.importantLimitations: This is a general guide. Tenancy laws vary by state jurisdictions. If your agreement was not registered, local civil courts or mediation centers may apply instead of the specialized Rent Authority.

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)

If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

response.informationThatMayApply: Under Supreme Court guidelines on police reforms and respective state Police Acts, citizens are protected against police abuse of authority. Independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) are mandated at the state and district levels to investigate serious misconduct.
response.why: A complaint can be filed before the PCA for grievances like custodial excess, grievous hurt, extortion, or abuse of power. CPGRAMS and departmental vigilance units also accept grievances. The complaint must contain specific officer details and supporting medical or media records.
whatYouMayDoNext: Record all incident details immediately, including date, time, officer names, belt numbers, and witness contacts.

documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs or video/audio recordings of the incident

response.importantLimitations: The PCA operates as a disciplinary audit authority. It can recommend suspensions or departmental actions but cannot directly award financial damages or cancel formal criminal charges (FIRs), which requires petitioning the High Court.

sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. The complaint must contain the name/designation of the officer, Station name, Date & Time of occurrence, Description of abuse, and supporting proof (such as medical reports, photos, or video recordings). Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

sessions.prompt: Garbage hasn't been collected in my street.

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting neglected municipal garbage collection or open waste dumping in your locality.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016, municipal authorities have a statutory duty to collect segregated waste daily, clear public street bins, and maintain clean public areas.

Submit a digital complaint ticket on the Swachhata App or the municipal e-district portal.

Resident petition letters signed by neighbors

sources.title: Security Deposit Return Guidelines under Model Tenancy Act
sources.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (Delhi State Rent Guidelines)
sources.content: According to Chapter IV of the Model Tenancy Act, the security deposit to be paid by the tenant in advance shall: (a) not exceed two months' rent in case of residential premises; and (b) not exceed six months' rent in case of non-residential premises. The security deposit shall be refunded to the tenant by the landlord at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making due deduction of any liability of the tenant (such as unpaid rent, utility bills, or cost of repairing tenant-caused structural damage). If the landlord fails to refund the security deposit or make adjustments within 30 days of the tenant vacating the premises, the tenant has the right to file a dispute petition before the Rent Authority or Rent Tribunal.

sessions.prompt: Police brutality (Incident Type: Excessive physical force, Location: Inside a police station, Evidence Available: Yes)

response.whatWeUnderstand: You are reporting police misconduct, which may include the use of excessive physical force, threat/intimidation, or illegal detention.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under Supreme Court guidelines on police reforms and respective state Police Acts, citizens are protected against police abuse of authority. Independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) are mandated at the state and district levels to investigate serious misconduct.
response.why: A complaint can be filed before the PCA for grievances like custodial excess, grievous hurt, extortion, or abuse of power. CPGRAMS and departmental vigilance units also accept grievances. The complaint must contain specific officer details and supporting medical or media records.
whatYouMayDoNext: Record all incident details immediately, including date, time, officer names, belt numbers, and witness contacts.
Seek medical attention immediately and secure a Medico-Legal Case (MLC) report if physical force was used.
File a written complaint with the Police Complaints Authority (PCA) or submit a grievance on CPGRAMS.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Photographs or video/audio recordings of the incident
Copy of any arbitrary fine slips or seizure memos
response.importantLimitations: The PCA operates as a disciplinary audit authority. It can recommend suspensions or departmental actions but cannot directly award financial damages or cancel formal criminal charges (FIRs), which requires petitioning the High Court.

sources.title: Filing Complaints Against Police Misconduct
sources.authority: Police Complaints Authority (PCA) Guidelines / Supreme Court Prakash Singh Reforms
sources.summary: Citizens can report police misconduct (excessive force, threat, extortion, illegal detention) to the independent state Police Complaints Authority.
sources.content: According to the Supreme Court directives on police reforms (Prakash Singh case), states are mandated to set up independent Police Complaints Authorities (PCA) at state and district levels. A citizen can file a written complaint before the PCA against police officers for: (a) excessive use of physical force; (b) illegal arrest or detention; (c) extortion or threat/intimidation; (d) custodial death or grievous hurt. The complaint must contain the name/designation of the officer, Station name, Date & Time of occurrence, Description of abuse, and supporting proof (such as medical reports, photos, or video recordings). Complaints must be submitted directly to the PCA registrar office or uploaded via the state online grievance portal.

sessions.prompt: My employer hasn't paid my wages (Issue details: Unpaid wages / salary delay & harassment? [urgent])

response.whatWeUnderstand: Your wages/salary remain unpaid or delayed by your employer, violating timely payment standards.
response.informationThatMayApply: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, employers are obligated to pay all wages in cash, cheque, or bank transfer in a timely manner (by the 7th of the following month for establishments with < 1000 workers).
response.why: Section 7 strictly limits authorized deductions. Withholding salary due to arbitrary disputes is illegal. Workers are entitled to receive full wages along with compensation for delayed payments by submitting claims to the regional labour department.
whatYouMayDoNext: Send a written salary demand letter to your employer via registered post/email.
Gather employment details, appointment letters, salary slips, and attendance sheets.
Submit a formal complaint claim under Section 15 of the Act to the Labour Commissioner.
documentsEvidenceThatMayHelp: Attendance records or emails showing work completed
response.importantLimitations: This Act primarily covers employees drawing salary below specified statutory thresholds. Higher-earning executives may need to seek recovery via standard civil suit litigation or arbitration panels.

sources.title: Timely Payment of Wages and Salary Guidelines
sources.authority: Ministry of Labour and Employment (Payment of Wages Act 1936)
sources.content: According to the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, every employer is responsible for the payment of all wages required to be paid to persons employed by him. Wages must be paid within a specified time limit: in establishments with fewer than 1,000 employees, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day of the following month, and in others before the 10th day. Payment must be made in currency notes, coins, or directly into the employee's bank account. Unauthorized deductions are strictly prohibited under Section 7 of the Act. In case of delayed or unpaid wages, employees are entitled to file a claim before the Labour Commissioner or the Authority appointed under Section 15 of the Act for recovery of wages along with compensation.
